title: Same-key memoization paired timing reconciliation
motivation: Two correctness-valid F-AHL28B CI executions straddled the frozen 75 percent warm-bind reduction threshold: 72.924 percent and 84.7847 percent. Selecting either run would be host-noise cherry-picking.
question: Under an in-process paired benchmark, does provider-local same-key reuse reduce adaptive bind/acquisition cost by at least the original frozen 75 percent relative to repeated shared-cache acquisition?
baseline: fresh provider acquisition against an already warm shared cache for the same exact hydraulic authority
candidate: same long-lived provider, exact same-key local representation reuse with step-duration fallback rebinding
correctness_gates: same-key local reuse does not increment shared-cache hit/miss/build/entry counts
changed step duration rebinds authoritative analytical fallback
changed hydraulic authority cannot take local fast path
restoring prior authority uses exact shared-cache key path

frozen_decision_rule.retain_F_AHL28B: median paired ratio <= 0.25, equivalent to at least 75 percent reduction
